# Python & DSA Practice 🐍

Welcome to my Python and Data Structures & Algorithms practice repository.

I'm building my programming fundamentals and problem-solving skills through consistent practice and hands-on coding.

## 📚 Topics Covered

# Day 1 — Python setup, syntax & core types
• Review: running Python in VS Code/terminal; print(), input(), comments, indentation.
• Learn variables, int/float/str/bool, type(), type conversion, arithmetic and comparison operators.
• Code: temperature converter, simple calculator, swap two variables, calculate average.
• DSA: understand what an algorithm is; trace a loop and count operations informally.
Output: 4 small programs. Explain the difference between = and ==, and between input text and a number.

# Day 2 — Conditions, loops & logic
• Learn if/elif/else, and/or/not, for, while, range(), break, continue.
• Practice nested conditions and loop tracing; watch for off-by-one errors.
• Code: even/odd, largest of three, multiplication table, sum 1..n, factorial using a loop.
• DSA: solve 3–4 beginner problems involving counting, min/max and repeated processing.
Checkpoint: write a loop without copying; explain its start, stop condition and update.

# Day 3 — Strings and lists
• Strings: indexing, slicing, len(), membership, immutability, common methods.
• Lists: indexing, slicing, append(), extend(), insert(), pop(), remove(), sort(), sorted().
• Code: reverse a string/list, count vowels, find largest and second largest, remove duplicates (simple approach).
• DSA: arrays/lists and linear traversal; solve 2 array + 2 string easy problems.
Checkpoint: explain index boundaries and the difference between sort() and sorted().

# Day 4 — Tuples, sets & dictionaries
• Learn tuple immutability; set uniqueness and membership; dict key/value access and updates.
• Practice in, get(), keys(), values(), items(), frequency counting.
• Code: character frequency, word counter, remove duplicates with a set, student marks dictionary.
• DSA: hashing idea—use a dictionary/set to avoid repeated nested searching.
Checkpoint: know when to choose list, tuple, set or dictionary.

# Day 5 — Functions, scope & recursion introduction
• Define functions; parameters, arguments, return vs print, default arguments and local variables.
• Break a larger problem into helper functions; test functions with different inputs.
• Recursion: base case, recursive case, call stack. Trace factorial and sum of n numbers.
• DSA: solve 2 function-based problems and 1 simple recursion problem.
Checkpoint: explain why a recursive function needs a base case. Do not rush into advanced recursion.

# Day 6 — Big-O, searching & sorting basics
• Learn time vs space complexity; O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²) at an intuitive level.
• Linear search and binary search; binary search requires sorted data.
• Understand built-in sorting and the basic idea of bubble/selection sort (conceptual, not memorisation).
• Practice: compare one loop vs nested loops; implement linear search and binary search.
Checkpoint: estimate complexity for simple snippets and explain why binary search is O(log n).

# Day 7 — Array patterns & weekly review
• Review traversal, running sum, min/max, in-place updates and two-pointer intuition.
• Solve: running sum, maximum element, move zeroes, remove duplicates from sorted array.
• Try two-sum with brute force first; record its time complexity.
• Revisit Days 1–6. Rebuild 2 programs without notes.
Milestone: 8–12 beginner problems attempted so far; list concepts that still feel unclear.

# Day 8 — Strings + two pointers
• Learn left/right pointers and when pointers move inward or forward.
• Practice palindrome check, reverse vowels or reverse string, valid palindrome (basic version).
• Compare a simple nested-loop solution with a two-pointer solution.
• For every solution, state the invariant: what do the pointers represent?
Checkpoint: explain why the pointers move and prove that no needed candidate is skipped.

# Day 9 — Hashing & frequency patterns
• Use dictionaries for counts, lookups and grouping; use sets for seen/not-seen checks.
• Practice Two Sum using a dictionary; first understand the brute-force version.
• Practice contains duplicate, valid anagram, first unique character / frequency count.
• Discuss average-case dictionary lookup as O(1), while remembering worst-case nuance.
Checkpoint: identify when a hash map can replace an inner loop.

# Day 10 — Prefix sums & sliding-window introduction
• Prefix sum: build cumulative totals and answer range-sum questions.
• Sliding window: maintain a window rather than recomputing every subarray.
• Practice: running/prefix sum, maximum sum of a fixed-size subarray, basic subarray sum.
• Draw the window on paper and trace each update.
Checkpoint: distinguish fixed-size window from a variable-size window. Focus on understanding, not speed.

# Day 11 — Binary search practice
• Review sorted arrays, mid calculation, low/high updates and termination.
• Implement binary search iteratively; test empty, one-element, absent and boundary targets.
• Solve: binary search, search insert position, first/last occurrence (with guidance).
• Explain the search interval after every iteration.
Checkpoint: write a correct binary search from a blank file and explain O(log n).

# Day 12 — Stacks, queues & recursion review
• Stack: LIFO; use list append()/pop(). Queue: FIFO; learn collections.deque.
• Practice valid parentheses and a simple queue simulation.
• Review recursion: factorial, power, GCD or print 1..n / n..1; trace calls by hand.
• Know what a linked list is conceptually; do not spend this day on advanced implementation.
Checkpoint: explain LIFO vs FIFO and identify a stack use case.

# Day 13 — Mixed DSA practice & debugging
• Choose 5–6 easy problems from arrays, strings, hashing, two pointers and binary search.
• For each: restate the problem, write examples, consider edge cases, choose an approach, code, test.
• After solving, write time and space complexity; compare with a better approach if one exists.
• Re-solve one previously difficult problem without looking at the old solution.
Checkpoint: focus on communicating your reasoning, not the number of questions completed.

# Day 14 — Mini assessment, revision & next steps
• 60-minute assessment: 1 string problem, 1 array problem, 1 dictionary/hash problem, 1 search/logic problem.
• For each question, explain brute force first, then improve if possible; test edge cases.
• Review your notes and create a personal Python syntax + DSA pattern sheet.
• Choose the next 4-week focus: arrays/hash maps, two pointers, sliding window, binary search, then stacks/queues and
recursion.

Finish line: a working foundation, a record of attempted problems, and a clear list of topics to continue—not mastery of all DSA.

## 🎯 Learning Goals

- Strengthen Python programming fundamentals.
- Understand time and space complexity.
- Improve logical thinking and problem-solving.
- Practice DSA problems regularly.
- Maintain consistency through hands-on coding.

## 📅 Progress

This repository is continuously updated as I learn new concepts and solve programming problems.
